The Opportunity

This is a chance to get hands-on experience verifying a next-generation processor architecture, working directly alongside our hardware team as we build supercomputer technology for the Edge.

You'll support the Design Verification team in documenting test plans, writing and debugging tests, and generating coverage for Quadric's GPNPU — gaining exposure to real verification methodologies used on CPU and GPU-class designs, and working closely with the architects and designers who built them.

Collaborate Across the Team

- Work closely with hardware architects and designers to understand design intent and clarify verification requirements.

- Communicate findings, blockers, and technical questions clearly to the team.

Within your internship, you'll:

- Build a working understanding of verification methodology for a CPU/GPU-class design.

- Contribute test plans, tests, and coverage that meaningfully support the team's verification effort.

- Develop hands-on fluency with SystemVerilog, SystemC, or C/C++ in a real verification environment.

Required

- Familiarity with verification methodologies for CPU or GPU designs.

- Proficient in either SystemVerilog, SystemC, or C/C++ (UVM is a plus).

- Prepared to collaborate with architects and designers to document test plans, write and debug tests, and generate coverage.

- Demonstrated capability in problem-solving, debugging, and clear technical communication.

- Exposure to assembly or low-level code generation.

- Adept with scripting languages like Python and using LLMs to get things done.

Pluralis Research works on Protocol Learning: training and serving large models in a fully decentralized way on small consumer-grade devices connected via the internet. Despite being dismissed as infeasible, we have made significant advances on this problem, most recently Agora, a permissionless run that pretrained an 8B model from scratch on consumer GPUs spread over the internet, with no single participant ever holding the full weights (tech report). While many of the core research problems have been solved, Protocol Learning unlocks a series of new challenges. For the mission in full, read A Third Path: Protocol Learning.

This setting breaks nearly every assumption of datacenter training and inference: communication-efficient training across different parallelism axes, fault tolerance as nodes join and drop mid-run, heterogeneous compute and networks, and robustness to malicious participants. Our published methods include Subspace Networks, Factored Gossip DiLoCo, AsyncMesh, and Sentinel.

As a Research Scientist Intern you join us for a 6-month, fixed-term research internship during your PhD, focused on publishing.
